summary: Klickitat County summit with a 1948 L-5 cab tower, removed or destroyed in 1958 and replaced by Sopelia; the summit is Yakama Nation land, so ask permission first.

facts.design: Wooden ring-connected tower with an L-5 cab (10 ft per register and firelookout.com; 12 ft per the 1948 sources)
facts.status_note: Tower removed or destroyed in 1958; the Sopelia lookout that replaced it burned in 2013; no source describes remains on the summit

access.note: Summit is officially on Yakama Nation land, and most of the reservation is closed to non-tribal visitors; ask the Yakama Nation before going

facts.agency: Yakama Nation (the register lists the Yakima Indian Reservation); tower built by the state Division of Forestry in 1948

events.note: A survey party described a temporary fire lookout on the summit: a rock windbreak and a field telephone

firelookout.com says the tower was destroyed in 1958; conflicts with the register's 'removed'
Sopelia lookout, an R-6 flat cab on concrete pillars, built the following year on a nearby site to replace the Simcoe Butte lookout
Nearby Sopelia lookout burned in a 2013 forest fire

notes_for_editor: Tower height disagrees: 10 ft (register, firelookout.com) versus 12 ft (Willhite, and the 1948 Annual Report quoted on Forest Lookouts); both kept in story. The 1958 end is 'removed' (register) versus 'destroyed' (firelookout.com). The 1948 Annual Report places the tower above Satus Pass while the 1948 newspaper names Frog (Conlee) Butte, which Willhite says is the same site; the record name Simcoe Butte is the register's. Land status: the register lists the Yakima Indian Reservation and Willhite says officially Yakama Nation; the Sopelia register says administered by the Bureau of Indian Affairs. Access is kept at 'permission' from the brief: Willhite's route is drive-up but crosses gated private land and Yakama land, so no visit guidance is given beyond asking permission. The record agency 'Yakima Indian Reservation' vs 'Yakama Nation' spelling is for a human to decide; not proposed as a correction. Search snippets mentioned a 1950 newspaper item naming a lookout (Joe Thorp) and a Lorena Butte claim that its 1954 cab replaced Simcoe; neither was read on a page, so neither is used. No staffing history for the 1948 tower was found in the sources read, so none is given. Research used 1 WebSearch and 6 page reads, within budget.
